description: Undo a finished build or removal job, a bulk write (write-N), a script run (script-14: the whole run, newest first), or the newest blueprint paste. Reports first; confirm: true undoes.

options.id: The job, the bulk write (write-N), the script run (script-14), or "paste" on its own; a list is undone newest first, in one report.
options.materials: The one holder every call pays from and refunds to. Default the job's own recorded source, else the player; never filled in by the verb layer.
options.confirm: true acts; left out, it reports.

-.summary: a job id (place-12, run-4, remove-3...), a bulk write (write-N), a script run (script-14: the whole run), or "paste" on its own

id.description: The job, the bulk write (write-N), the script run (script-14), or "paste" on its own; a list is undone newest first, in one report.

materials.description: The one holder every call pays from and refunds to. Default the job's own recorded source, else the player; never filled in by the verb layer.

refund_to.description: Where removals' refunds go. Default nothing after a free placement, else each tool's own list.

allow.description: Bulk writes: overwrite: write a previous value back even where it drifted since.

from_step.description: Bulk writes: go on from this step after a refused one.

text: A bulk write undo lists every step with its mark: build and removal jobs [undo] (undo of each, newest first); swap jobs [cannot undo: change job]; logic writes of held settings, memory, label, paint, pins, uplink and genes [undo] (previous values written back); action and pulse logic types [cannot undo: action]; battery [undo: restores the value, not what happened since]; item slot moves [undo] unless merged; chip source, run controls, screen presses, gas moves, player moves, trades, console commands and store moves [cannot undo].

A script run (script-14) is reverted whole, newest first, each target restored to its value before the run; jobs still in flight at a stop are included once they settle, and groups that cannot be undone are named [cannot undo]. Each target is compared with the run's last written value: where it changed since (the user, a chip, another run), the target is reported and not written unless allow: ["overwrite"]. Undo of a running run is refused: stop it first (server {what: "stop", id}). Past the memory bound undo answers undo_expired, naming what it can no longer revert.
